_about: One primary URL per head intent for the 11 money markets.
This file records INTENT ONLY. It is not a routing surface and nothing in this
repository consumes it at request time. vercel.json is likewise not a routing
surface: the site is served by GitHub Pages behind Cloudflare, GitHub Pages does
not read vercel.json, and every 301 observed on the live site is executed at the
Cloudflare edge. vercel.json is an accurate MIRROR of that edge configuration
(69/69 rules verified live on 2026-07-29, zero drift, zero live 301s absent from
the file) but editing it deploys nothing. Redirect changes must be applied
externally -- see .github/cloudflare/RUNBOOK.md.
Two intents per market. 'commercial-glazing' (broad contractor intent) and
'storefront' (storefront installation intent) are SEPARATE head intents with
SEPARATE primaries. Collapsing them into one URL was the error in the superseded
plan on branch fix/canonical-cannibalization-money-markets.
A 'storefront-glazier-{city}-florida/' page is a legitimate primary for the
storefront intent and must NEVER be the primary for the broad commercial-glazing
intent. Where the live edge currently routes a broad-intent slug into one, that
is recorded as a required external redirect, not fixed in-repo.
No entry here is derived from Google Search Console. No GSC export exists in this
workspace and the measurement layer added by PR #20 has never run (it needs the
GSC_SA_JSON secret). Every entry is therefore marked 'ratified' only when two
independent in-workspace sources agree AND acting on it moves no URL that is
known to rank; everything else is 'gsc-gated' and must not be actioned until
the GSC baseline exists.

status_legend.ratified: Two independent workspace sources agree and no known-ranking URL moves. Safe to enforce.
status_legend.frozen: Must not change under any circumstances in this workstream. Enforced as a hard gate.
status_legend.gsc-gated: A defensible target exists but acting on it flips a primary. Blocked on a GSC baseline.
status_legend.blocked-no-primary: No page on disk can hold this intent. Blocked on content creation, not on routing.
status_legend.owned-elsewhere: Files are owned by another open PR. Out of scope here to avoid conflicting edits.

Two freeze MODES. Every prefix above is byte-frozen -- must be byte-identical to
the base ref -- EXCEPT the ones listed in semantic_freeze below, which are frozen
field by field instead. See semantic_freeze._about for why the root differs.

_about: A byte freeze on '/' protects the ranking signals, but it also forbids every
harmless body addition, because it cannot tell a repointed canonical from a new
paragraph. The root is the site's main hub; freezing it byte-for-byte blocks
ordinary internal-linking work for the whole duration of the WPB freeze, and the
WPB freeze has no end date -- it lifts when a GSC baseline exists.
The freeze's actual purpose is that the root must keep ranking #1 in the map pack
for the WPB Google Business Profile. What carries that is a specific, listable set
of fields. So the root is frozen on those fields and open elsewhere: body-only
additions of truthful contextual service and market navigation are permitted, and
every protected field must be identical to the base ref.
The dedicated WPB pages stay BYTE-frozen. They are the four contested candidates
for the organic #1 plus their support pages; the ranking URL among them is
unknown, so nothing about them may move, including body copy.

/.reason: Root is the WPB Google Business Profile landing page (#1 map pack). Its identity and ranking signals are frozen; its body is not.

protected_fields.title: <title> text, exact.
protected_fields.meta-robots: meta[name=robots] content, exact. ABSENT is a protected value -- adding any robots directive fails.
protected_fields.h1: The ordered list of H1 texts, exact. The H1 is owner-settled.
protected_fields.og:title: meta[property=og:title] content, exact.
protected_fields.schema-identity: For every JSON-LD node typed Organization, LocalBusiness, HomeAndConstructionBusiness or WebSite: the @id set is fixed, and each node's @type, name, legalName, url, telephone, address, geo, sameAs, areaServed and logo are fixed. This is the NAP and entity identity the map pack resolves against, including the #localbusiness-west-palm-beach node.
protected_fields.wpb-links: Every (href, anchor text) pair on the base version whose target is a byte-frozen WPB URL must still be present. Removal or rewording fails.
protected_fields.wpb-text: Every visible-text segment on the base version that mentions West Palm Beach must still be present. Removal or rewording fails.

permitted: Body-only additions of truthful contextual service and market navigation.
New sections, new in-page anchors, new internal links, new nav entries.
Anything at all that leaves every protected field byte-identical.
warns_but_does_not_block: Adding a NEW link from the root to a byte-frozen WPB URL. It removes nothing, so
it is permitted, but it does nudge one of the four contested candidates ahead of
the others -- which is the decision the freeze exists to defer. The gate lists
each one so a reviewer sees it rather than discovering it later.
